newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, DAVENPORT ADVANCE AT EVERT CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, DAVENPORT ADVANCE AT EVERT CUP.

text.p: Top seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, looking to end a 10-month title drought, scored a 6-4 6-2 second-round win over Silvia Farina of Italy at the Evert Cup tennis tournament on Saturday.
Fourth-seeded Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport also moved smoothly into the third round with a solid 6-4 6-0 win over 78th-ranked fellow American Tami Whitlinger-Jones.
But eighth-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer failed to get out of the second round, becoming one of the day's two seeded casualties.
Despite a fast start, the 13th-ranked Coetzer was bounced 1-6 7-5 7-5 by 52nd-ranked Florencia Labat of Argentina.
American Lisa Raymond, the 16th seed, was ousted 5-7 6-3 6-4 by 33rd-ranked Sadrine Testud of France.

The fourth-ranked Sanchez is hoping to use this tournament to turn around her frustrating 1996 fortunes. The Spaniand has not won since the Hamburg tournament last May, reaching nine finals in 1996 but collecting just two titles.

"Last year I played some very tough matches, especially in the Grand Slam finals, and it's hard for an athlete to recover from that," said Sanchez, who suffered devastating final-round defeats to Steffi Graf in the French Open and Wimbledon and to Davenport at the Olympics.

In the first set, the 40th-ranked Farina was able to pressure Sanchez by holding her first four service games easily. But the Italian failed to convert three break opportunities in the set and Sanchez ended it by taking the final two games.
The top seed was more forceful in the second set, racing out to a commanding 5-1 lead.
Although Farina had five additional chances to break Sanchez in the second set, she was no more successful with her opportunities than in the first set.
"She started playing pretty good and I started slow," Sanchez said. "Once I started getting more into the match, I tried to take the ball from her and move it around more."
The eighth-ranked Davenport was ahead 4-1, 40-0 on Whitlinger-Jones's serve in the sixth game when she suffered a lapse that prolonged the first set.
After securing the first set, Davenport thoroughly dominated the second, winning 24 of the 29 points played.
"I stayed more concentrated on the match in the second set," Davenport said. "I was able to keep focused, go for the right shots and go for great shots."
